title: Binary & data representation
hook: A byte is just eight bits. What those bits mean depends entirely on who is reading them.

steps.caption: Here’s one byte — the same eight bits, sitting still.

nodeCaptions.byte: Bits don’t come with a label. Meaning is assigned by the program.
nodeCaptions.as-num: Read as an integer, this might be 65.

steps.caption: Read the same bits as text (ASCII/UTF-8) and you get the letter A.

nodeCaptions.as-text: Encodings map bit patterns to characters. Same bits, different agreement.

steps.caption: Hand those bits to the CPU as an instruction and they become an operation to run.

nodeCaptions.as-op: Machine code is still just bits — the CPU’s decoder decides what they mean.

takeaways: Bits are raw. Types, encodings, and instruction sets are agreements about meaning.
The same byte can be a number, a letter, or an instruction depending on context.
Bugs often come from reading bits with the wrong agreement.

quiz.question: What decides whether a byte is a number or a letter?
choices: The program’s agreement about how to interpret those bits
Bytes that look like letters can’t be numbers
quiz.explanation: Representation is interpretation. Nothing in the byte itself says “I am text.”
